plan.notes: Source: Barnard College Chemistry Department official 'Suggested Four-Year Program' for the Chemistry major ('CHEM 2017 and beyond', for students completing General Chemistry in the first year). Hand-transcribed 2026-10-01. The department's first-year-start PDF (formerly at chemistry.barnard.edu/sites/default/files/inline-files/CHEM 2017 and beyond Gen Chem FY Suggested Program.pdf) was removed from the live site in 2026 (Fall 2026 schedule information moved to the student Portal); the table was recovered from the search-engine cache of the official PDF and cross-checked against the Barnard College Catalogue 2025-2026 (catalog.barnard.edu), whose Chemistry major requirements (at least 61.5 credits: 46.5 chemistry + 6.0 math + 9.0 physics) match every course, credit value, and prerequisite shown here. The department's sophomore-start variant ('Suggested program for students who complete General Chemistry in sophomore year') remains live at barnard.edu and supplied the official Notes 1-5 text quoted below; it is not separately seeded. Department Notes (verbatim from the official suggested-program document): Note 1. Two semesters of math after entering college, including Calculus I and II are required. Students having AP credit for 1 or 2 semesters of calculus will fulfill this requirement with additional mathematics, statistics, or computer science courses. For the Class of 2021 and beyond, students must complete through Calculus II, including two math courses while a student at Barnard. At least one of the courses taken at Barnard must be a calculus class. Note 2. The Barnard physics sequence (PHYS BC2001x-2002y) is strongly recommended. Any calculus-based Columbia sequence, with two semesters of laboratory work, is acceptable (1401-2, 1601-2, but not 1201-2). Consult with your advisor to ensure proper laboratory placement. For greater coverage of basic physics, PHYS BC3001x (Waves and Optics) is recommended. Note 3. One elective course is required. A list of approved advanced lecture and/or lab courses at Barnard or Columbia is available. Note 4. Senior Honors Thesis (CHEM BC3901/3902) or Guided Research (CHEM BC3599) at Barnard, Columbia, or elsewhere. Note 5. Completion of CHEM BC3282 (Biological Chemistry) is required to receive an American Chemical Society certified degree. It is not required for the major. Scope: the published program schedules major-requirement courses only; Barnard Foundations (general education) requirements and additional electives needed to reach the 122-point BA are chosen by the student with the adviser and are not part of the published sequence, so total_credits (71.5) is the sum of the published major-course sequence, not the full degree. It exceeds the catalog's 61.5-credit major minimum because the published program includes the optional junior-fall elective (the department encourages considering an elective in junior fall) and CHEM BC3282 (ACS-certification course, optional for the major). Course codes: the x/y suffixes in the department document denote fall/spring offerings and are dropped here (catalog codes carry no term suffix). external_prereqs: 'Algebra' (CHEM BC2001 prerequisite: Math SAT I score of 600 or instructor permission for first-year students, per the catalog course description); 'BIOL BC1502' (prerequisite of the optional ACS-certification course CHEM BC3282, otherwise not in this plan); 'MATH UN1201' (alternative prerequisite 'MATH UN1102 or 1201' for the physical chemistry courses; the plan schedules MATH UN1102).
